title: Comparatives and Superlatives Quiz 4
description: Use as ... as, the more ... the more, and choose the correct form in context.
instructions: Comparatives and Superlatives: Equal comparisons and mixed forms.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence means the same as 'Anna is as tall as Ben'?
options: Anna is taller than Ben.
Ben is taller than Anna.
Anna is the tallest girl.
Anna and Ben are the same height.
questions.explanation: As ... as shows equality. Watch out: it is not a comparative.

questions.question: He runs as {{1}} as I do. (fast)
questions.explanation: After as ... as, the basic adjective or adverb is used. Watch out: not faster.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is not as older as his brother.
He is not as old as his brother.
He is not as old than his brother.
He is not so older as his brother.
questions.explanation: Not as + basic adjective + as. Watch out: than does not go with as.

questions.question: In 'as tall as', we use the basic form of the adjective, not the comparative.
questions.explanation: The adjective does not change: as tall as. Watch out: as taller as is wrong.

questions.question: The more you practise, the {{1}} you become. (good)
questions.explanation: The pattern the more ..., the more ... uses comparatives. Watch out: good becomes better.

questions.question: Complete: 'It is getting ___ every day.'
options: colder and colder
cold and colder
the coldest and coldest
more cold and more cold
questions.explanation: A change that increases uses comparative and comparative. Watch out: cold is short, so no more.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is the better book I have ever read.
This is a better book I have ever read.
This is the best book I have ever read.
This is best book I have ever read.
questions.explanation: With ever, we use the superlative with the. Watch out: the better is only for two things.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: She is taller that her sister.
accepted: She is taller than her sister.
She is taller than her sister
questions.explanation: Comparatives need than, not that. Watch out: one letter changes the meaning.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is youngest of the three brothers.
He is the youngest of the three brothers.
He is the most young of the three brothers.
He is the younger of the three brothers.
questions.explanation: Three or more means the superlative. Watch out: young is short, so youngest.

questions.question: Match each structure with its use.
right: the top of three or more
questions.explanation: Each structure has its meaning. Watch out: the superlative needs three or more things.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The superlative comes after the, and the time or place follows.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: He is as stronger as an ox.
This is the most cheapest of all.
This is the cheapest of all.
He is as strong as an ox.
questions.explanation: As + basic adjective + as, and one superlative marker only. Watch out: more or most plus -er or -est is wrong.
